title: Volunteering for the Navy band at seventeen
summary: Enlisting after a Navy bandmaster recruited him; Chief Edwards; segregated unit at Guantanamo Bay.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah. Oh, so when did you, were you drafted into the?
Into the Navy? No. World War II.

World War II, I was seventeen years old, and I was playing in Mottville, Louisiana, and there was a Navy bandmaster going around recruiting musicians to play in the Navy band to be stationed here in New Orleans. And I said, now I'm seventeen years old and I didn't have to register for the service, because you had to register at eighteen, I was only seventeen. I said, now if I wait another year, they might put me in the Army. So I got a chance to play with the Navy band, and I have to fight. So I volunteered. But my mother and father had to sign for me. So I got into the Navy, and I enjoyed it, because I learned a lot about music. And we had to practice. The old band director we had, he was very particular about his music. He liked for it to be played correctly.
Who was the band director? Edwards.
Now I've forgotten his first name, because everybody called him Chief, Chief Edwards. He's an old climate player from North Carolina.
Now you were in a segregated unit, right?
Oh yeah, at that time, the whole service was segregated. Where were you stationed?
Oh, okay. Did you get to travel around Cuba, or was it during that time? No. Right on the base. And the...
The... The... The... The... The... The... The...
